description: Store owners: wait a day after you write your page, open it on your phone and read only the first screen. Write down every guess you had to make. Can a stranger tell what it is, who it's for and why this one? Every guess is one fix.
alt_text: Phone mock of a product page with the first screen marked, and 4 steps of the stranger test: wait a day, open it on your phone, read only the first screen, write down every guess.

title: Digital Product Mistakes: 6 Traps That Stop Most First Products
description: Six traps that stop most first digital products: the exciting idea, the polite yes, the big first version, the broad keyword, every channel at once, and changing everything at the same time. Which one is yours? Save this as a checklist. How to avoid all 6: The Digital Product System: From Idea to Sales.
alt_text: Grid of 6 common first digital product traps: the exciting idea, the polite yes, the big first version, the broad keyword, every channel at once, changing everything.

title: How to Build Your First Digital Product: The Minimum Useful Version
description: Building product number one? Skip more pages and more bonuses and build one complete result for the buyer. Check 4 boxes: it delivers one complete outcome, gives a first result in the first session, is buildable in about 2 weeks of your hours, and every part serves the outcome. Product Blueprint inside The Digital Product System: From Idea to Sales.
alt_text: Checklist for a minimum useful first digital product: delivers one complete outcome, first result in the first session, buildable in about 2 weeks, every part serves the outcome.

title: Blog Post Ending Ideas: End Every Post With One Next Step
description: Writing your first posts? Swap thanks for reading for one clear next step, like want the checklist from this post, it's free here. The reader just got value, so the next step feels natural, not pushy. Try it on your next post.
alt_text: Before and after blog post endings: thanks for reading crossed out, replaced with want the checklist from this post, it's free here, with a note on why it works.

title: Track Your Gumroad Product Page Improvements Over Time
description: Gumroad sellers: see the trend, not a guess. Without tracking it's I changed something, I think it helped. With the TRACKER, every round is logged and the trend shows on a chart. TRACKER with charts is in the PRO version of the AI Shopping Readiness Kit.
alt_text: Example line chart of a product page score rising over 5 rounds, with a comparison of guessing without tracking and logging every round with the TRACKER. AI Shopping Readiness Kit PRO.

title: Etsy Listing Description Tips: Use Words From Real Reviews
description: Etsy and Gumroad sellers: your best listing words are in other people's reviews. Read the 1 to 3 star reviews of similar products, note the exact words buyers use, like I couldn't edit it or I wish it showed an example, then answer them in your first lines, your FAQ and your what's inside list.
alt_text: Three example low-star reviews with highlighted buyer phrases, and where to use those words on your page: first lines, FAQ answers and what's inside list.

title: Digital Product Launch Checklist: 6 Things to Check Before Launch Week
description: Launching soon? Check six things: idea scored 65 or more, validation 4 to 5 yes checked from your desk, self-test passed, Search Console verified, two channels chosen, and checkout tested on a phone. One glance shows what's missing. Launch Playbook inside The Digital Product System: From Idea to Sales.
alt_text: Launch week checklist for a digital product: idea scored 65 plus, validation 4 to 5 yes, self-test passed, Search Console verified, two channels chosen, checkout tested on a phone.

title: AI Shopping Readiness Kit: What's Inside, Tab by Tab
description: Store owners: here's what's inside, tab by tab. Start and field guide, a worked example, BEFORE with 25 questions, SETUP, 13 AI tests, RESULTS, IMPROVE with a master prompt, COPY STUDIO, AFTER, and 10 core prompts. PRO adds 5 more tabs. For Shopify, Etsy, Gumroad and any online store.
alt_text: Map of 10 tabs inside the AI Shopping Readiness Kit Standard: start, worked example, before, setup, AI tests, results, improve, copy studio, after, prompts, colour-coded by start, measure and test, fix, compare.

title: How to Sell Digital Products Without an Audience: The 10-Question Test
description: No audience yet? Write 10 specific questions the people you want to help type into search. 10 or more? Lead with search, buyers are already looking. Fewer? Make your group more specific and try again. Save it and fill it in.
alt_text: Notepad template for the 10-question search test with 3 example questions for short-stay hosts filled in and 7 blank lines, plus results: 10 or more lead with search, fewer make your group more specific.

title: Digital Product Research: Collect Real Problems in Their Own Words
description: Finding your first idea? Collect real problems from 1 to 3 star reviews, how do I threads, search autocomplete and homemade fixes. Log where you found each one, their exact words and any workaround. Aim for about 20, then score the best one. Research Log inside The Digital Product System: From Idea to Sales.
alt_text: Four places to find real problems, reviews, threads, autocomplete and homemade fixes, with an example research log table of where, their exact words and workaround, and a goal of about 20 problems.

title: How to Write Alt Text for Product Images: A Simple Formula
description: Store owners: your photos can't speak, your alt text can. AI assistants and screen readers read it, and most stores leave it empty. Use this formula: what it is, plus a key detail, plus who or what it's for. Example: soy candle in an amber glass jar, lavender scent, 40-hour burn, for a calm bedroom. One line per photo.
alt_text: Alt text formula for product images: what it is plus key detail plus who or what for, with an example for a soy candle in an amber glass jar.

title: Product Page Improvement Plan: From Weak Spots to a Rewrite
description: Store owners: the RESULTS tab lists your weak spots, and IMPROVE turns them into a step-by-step plan, fix this first, then this, plus one master prompt for the rewrite that uses your audit answers. Measure, plan, rewrite, compare. AI Shopping Readiness Kit.
alt_text: Diagram from RESULTS weak spots to an IMPROVE step-by-step plan, plus one master prompt for the rewrite, and the flow measure, plan, rewrite, compare. AI Shopping Readiness Kit.

title: Digital Product Templates for Google Sheets and Excel
description: No Excel? No problem. All 12 templates open in Google Sheets too, free in your browser. The scores calculate themselves, each template has a filled-in example, and it all lives in one workbook from first idea to launch. Inside The Digital Product System: From Idea to Sales.
alt_text: Excel or Google Sheets icons with three points: the scores calculate themselves, each template has a filled-in example, from first idea to launch in one workbook.

title: How to Make a Pinterest Pin People Save: 5 Parts
description: New to Pinterest? A pin people save has 5 parts: a tall 2:3 size like 1000 by 1500, a big clear headline readable on a phone, a keyword title with the words people search, content useful on its own like a checklist or steps, and a link to a page about the same thing. Save this and make your first pin.
alt_text: Anatomy of a Pinterest pin with 5 labeled parts: tall 2:3 size, big clear headline, keyword title, useful on its own, matching link.

title: Product Page Audit for WooCommerce, Wix, Squarespace and Etsy
description: WooCommerce, Wix and Squarespace sellers: not on Shopify? It still works. The AI Shopping Readiness Kit works on Etsy, your own site and Shopify too, for digital or physical products. Audit any product page with 25 questions, test it with 13 ready AI prompts, fix it, then score it again.
alt_text: Grid of store platforms, WooCommerce, Etsy, Wix, Squarespace, your own site and Shopify, with digital and physical products, and three kit steps: audit with 25 questions, test with 13 AI prompts, fix and score again.

title: Product Description Tip: Add a Not for You If Line
description: Gumroad and Etsy sellers: add a not for you if line under who it's for. The right buyers feel seen, the wrong ones leave before they're disappointed, and it builds trust. Example for a fictional planner template: for you if you sell printable planners, not for you if you need a physical planner. Write yours in 5 minutes.
alt_text: Two columns for a fictional planner template: for you if you sell printable planners, want a ready layout, edit in Canva; not for you if you need a physical planner, want to design from zero, don't use Canva.

title: Blog Post Outline Template: Plan an Article in 5 Lines
description: Blank page again? Plan one helpful article in 5 lines: the search phrase, the reader's real question, 3 points that answer it, one worked example, and one next step. Write the 5 lines first and the writing gets easy after. Content Brief inside The Digital Product System: From Idea to Sales.
alt_text: Five-line article plan: the search phrase, the reader's real question, 3 points that answer it, one worked example, one next step, with handwritten examples.

title: Etsy Listing Details Table: Format, Size, Pages, Editable
description: Etsy sellers: buyers and AI scan the details first. Pull the facts out of your paragraph into a table: format, size, pages, editable or not, and best for. COPY STUDIO in the AI Shopping Readiness Kit builds your title, opening lines, details table and FAQ.
alt_text: Before and after for an Etsy listing: details hidden in a paragraph, then an example details table with format, size, pages, editable and best for.

title: What to Post When You Sell Digital Products: 5 Post Ideas
description: Nothing to post today? One product gives you 5 posts: a checklist from inside it, a before and after, the mistake it fixes, a 3-step mini how-to, and how you built it. Save this for your next blank day.
alt_text: Five post ideas from one digital product: a checklist from inside it, a before and after, the mistake it fixes, a 3-step mini how-to, how you built it.

title: Test Your Digital Product Idea Before You Build: A Waitlist Story
description: The course Maya almost built, a fictional example from inside the system. Maya runs two short-stay apartments and first planned a video course. A waitlist for the course got 4 sign-ups from 120 visitors; a ready-to-use host kit got 19 from 140. One small test changed her plan before she built anything. Follow Maya's full journey in The Digital Product System: From Idea to Sales.
alt_text: Fictional example: Maya compared two waitlists, a video course with 4 sign-ups from 120 visitors and a ready-to-use host kit with 19 sign-ups from 140 visitors, and changed her plan before building.

title: Gumroad Tip: Add a Start Here Page to Every Download
description: Gumroad sellers: put a Start Here page in every download. Name it 00 so it shows first, and keep it to one page: what's in the folder, which file to open first, how to get the first result, and where to ask a question. Fewer confused buyers, a better first impression.
alt_text: Product download folder with a 00 Start Here file on top, and what goes on it: what's in the folder, which file to open first, how to get the first result, where to ask a question.

title: Test Your Shopify Store With Free ChatGPT: 13 Ready AI Tests
description: Shopify owners: no paid AI needed, the free ChatGPT is enough. Run 13 ready AI tests on your product page, copy, paste and note the answer. Any AI assistant works; one rule, use the same one every time so your before and after are fair. AI Shopping Readiness Kit.
alt_text: Big number 13 ready AI tests for Shopify owners, free ChatGPT and any AI assistant work, with the rule to use the same assistant every time. AI Shopping Readiness Kit.

title: How to Check Demand for a Digital Product in 30 Minutes (Free)
description: Have an idea? Run the free 30-minute demand check. 10 minutes: is interest steady on Google Trends? 10 minutes: do people buy similar things on Gumroad and Etsy? 10 minutes: what do buyers dislike in 1 to 3 star reviews? No calls, no interviews, just your desk. Part of the Fast Start in The Digital Product System: From Idea to Sales.
alt_text: Three 10-minute blocks of a free demand check: steady interest on Google Trends, similar products on Gumroad and Etsy, buyer complaints in 1 to 3 star reviews.

title: How to Name a Digital Product: Result + Format + Who It's For
description: Naming your first product? Name it so people get it at first read: the result, plus the format, plus who it's for. Example names: Guest-Ready Host Kit for Short-Stay Hosts, Weekly Budget Spreadsheet for Students, Client Onboarding Templates for Freelancers. Clear beats clever, every time.
alt_text: Digital product naming formula, the result plus the format plus for who, with three example names replacing vague names like The Calm Collection.

title: Does ChatGPT Describe Your Shopify Product Correctly? Quick Test
description: Shopify owners: ask an AI assistant what is your product and who is it for. In this example it says a planner for teachers, but it's really a shift planner for nurses. A wrong answer means an unclear page: name the buyer and the use in your first lines, then ask again. Understanding tests in the AI Shopping Readiness Kit.
alt_text: Example chat where AI describes a product as a planner for teachers while it's really a shift planner for nurses, with the fix: name the buyer and the use in your first lines.

title: How to Refresh an Old Etsy or Gumroad Listing in 4 Steps
description: Etsy and Gumroad sellers: refresh an old listing before you make a new one. Update the title with the words buyers search, the first lines with who it's for and what they get, the preview image with one real page from inside, and one FAQ answer for the doubt you hear most. One at a time: change one, wait for about 100 visits, then change the next.
alt_text: Four ways to refresh an old listing: title, first lines, preview image, one FAQ, with the rule to change one thing at a time and wait for about 100 visits.

title: How to Test Your Digital Product Before Launch: The Self-Test
description: Built your first product? You can't see your own gaps, so become a stranger. Wait a day, follow only your written steps like a brand-new buyer, and note every guess, each one is a missing line. It's ready when you reach the first result using only your steps and the 12-point check passes. Product Blueprint inside The Digital Product System: From Idea to Sales.
alt_text: Self-test steps for a new digital product: wait a day, follow only your written steps, note every guess; ready when you reach the first result and the 12-point check passes.

title: Does ChatGPT Recommend Your Digital Product? Try This Prompt
description: Digital product sellers: when shoppers ask AI to compare, are you on the list? Try asking: what are the best [product type] for [buyer], compare 3 options. Check if you were on the list and if the reason was right. Recommendation tests are inside the AI Shopping Readiness Kit.
alt_text: Prompt asking AI to compare the best product type for a buyer, an example answer list with your product as a question mark, and two checks: were you on the list, was the reason right.

title: How to Describe Your Digital Product in One Sentence
description: Before you build a digital product, write its one-sentence promise: helps [who] [do what] without [the pain]. Example: helps new short-stay hosts welcome guests with a ready kit without writing everything from scratch. If you can't write it yet, your product idea isn't clear yet. A simple first step for beginners, with a special skill or without one.
alt_text: Fill-in formula for a digital product promise, helps who do what without the pain, with two labeled example sentences for short-stay hosts and freelancers.

title: Is Your Product Page Ready for AI Shopping? 5 Quick Yes/No Checks
description: Store owners: check your product page for AI shopping assistants like ChatGPT. Does your title say what it is? Does the first line name the buyer? Are key details written in text, not only in photos? Does your FAQ answer real doubts? Does AI find you without your store name? Any no is your starting point. The AI Shopping Readiness Kit goes deeper with a 25-question audit and 13 AI tests.
alt_text: Five yes or no checks for an AI-ready product page, covering title, buyer, details in text, FAQ and being found without your store name, from the AI Shopping Readiness Kit.

title: Better Product Descriptions: 3 Swaps From Vague to Specific
description: Gumroad and Etsy sellers: specific words beat vague ones in product descriptions. Swap 'lots of templates' for the real count, 'easy to use' for what the buyer actually does, and 'saves you time' for the result they get. Example lines only, so use your own real details. Buyers trust what they can check.
alt_text: Three before and after swaps for product descriptions, vague phrases crossed out and replaced with specific example lines, for Gumroad and Etsy sellers.

title: When to Change Your Sales Page: Wait for About 100 Visitors
description: Just launched your digital product? Ten visitors is too soon to rewrite your sales page. Wait for about 100 visitors, then change one thing at a time so you know what made the difference. This comes from the Convert and Improve steps in The Digital Product System: From Idea to Sales.
alt_text: Grid of visitor dots showing 10 visitors as a guess and about 100 as a pattern, with advice to change one thing at a time on a digital product sales page.

title: Digital Product Idea Not Working? What to Do After Each Score
description: A low idea score isn't the end, it tells you what to do next. Idea Scorecard: 65 or more, test it; lower, change one thing or pick another idea. Validation Checklist: 4 to 5 yes, build it; 2 to 3, change the offer; 0 to 1, try another group or idea. Every gate in The Digital Product System: From Idea to Sales ends with a clear next step.
alt_text: Decision guide for two gates of The Digital Product System, the Idea Scorecard and the Validation Checklist, showing the next step for each score range.

title: Free Keyword Research on Pinterest: Use the Search Suggestions
description: Free keyword research for beginners, right inside Pinterest. Type your topic in the search bar and don't press enter. Screenshot the suggestions that appear, then use those exact words in your pin titles and descriptions. Their words become your keywords. Takes about two minutes.
alt_text: Pinterest search bar with example suggestion bubbles and three steps for free keyword research, type the topic, screenshot the suggestions, use the words in pin titles.

title: Did Your Product Page Improve? Score It Again and Compare
description: Store owners: rewrote your product page and not sure it's better? The AFTER tab in the AI Shopping Readiness Kit asks the same 25 questions again, so you compare your before and after scores section by section, not by feeling.
alt_text: Blank before and after score table with sections and a total out of 100, showing how the AFTER tab in the AI Shopping Readiness Kit compares the same 25 questions.

title: How to Organize Your Digital Product Shop: By Problem, Not File Type
description: Shop owners: sort your shop sections by the buyer's problem, not by file type. Instead of PDFs, spreadsheets and Canva files, try sections like plan your week, track your money or welcome new clients. Example sections only. Buyers arrive with a problem, so let them find it first.
alt_text: Comparison of shop sections grouped by format versus grouped by buyer problem, with example section names for a digital product shop.

title: Can ChatGPT Find Your Store Without Your Name? 5 Blind Tests
description: Shopify owners: a blind test asks AI for your product type, never your store name, like a shopper who has never heard of you. If AI only finds you when you type your name, new shoppers won't see you. The AI Shopping Readiness Kit includes 5 blind discovery tests as part of its 13 AI tests.
alt_text: Explainer of blind AI discovery tests, asking for a product type without the store name, with five numbered blind tests from the AI Shopping Readiness Kit.

title: How Often to Review Your Marketing Channels: Every 8 Weeks
description: Posting on two channels? Don't judge them every day. Review every 8 weeks and decide: keep what brings visits or sign-ups, change one thing where people see but don't click, and stop what doesn't move to free those hours. Part of the weekly system in The Digital Product System: From Idea to Sales.
alt_text: Eight-week timeline ending in a review, with keep, change and stop decisions for marketing channels when selling digital products.

title: Content Marketing for Beginners: Write Once, Share 4 Ways
description: Short on time? Write one helpful article that answers one real question, then share it four ways: a pin with the steps, a short answer in a thread where it's asked, one tip in an email, and the full article on Medium. One idea, four chances to be found, with no ads.
alt_text: One helpful article turned into four pieces of content, a pin, a thread answer, an email and a Medium post, for beginners selling digital products.

title: Product Page Audit for Gumroad Sellers: Measure, Test, Fix, Compare
description: Gumroad sellers: one full round for your product page. Measure with 25 questions and a score out of 100. Run 13 ready AI tests and note what AI says. Fix the weakest parts first. Then score again and compare. Standard is one full round of the AI Shopping Readiness Kit, and PRO keeps going for 30 days.
alt_text: Four-step loop for a product page, measure, test, fix and compare, from the AI Shopping Readiness Kit, with Standard as one full round and PRO for 30 days.

title: Can Buyers Find Your Product? Search for It Like a Stranger
description: Store owners: search for your own product without your shop name, on Google, Pinterest and your marketplace. If you show up, note the exact words that found you and use them more. If you don't, look at who does and what words are in their titles. Five minutes, no tools.
alt_text: Search bar with the shop name crossed out, three places to search, and what to do if your product shows up or doesn't, for store owners.

title: From Idea to First Digital Product: Maya's Journey Through 6 Gates
description: Follow Maya, a fictional example from inside The Digital Product System: From Idea to Sales. She scored her host-kit idea at 75 and tested it, moved her Validation Checklist from 2 out of 5 to 5 out of 5 by changing the offer, built a small Guest-Ready Host Kit, found keywords in hosts' own questions, wrote a product page with 5 welcome emails, and improved one change at a time.
alt_text: Six-gate journey of Maya, a fictional example, from Find and Prove to Build, Be Found, Convert and Improve, in The Digital Product System.

title: Weekly Routine for Digital Product Sellers: The 30-Minute Friday Check
description: Set a timer for 30 minutes every Friday. Ten minutes: what got the most views this week? Ten minutes: what got saves, clicks or sign-ups? Ten minutes: pick one thing to do more of next week. Part of the weekly routine in The Digital Product System: From Idea to Sales.
alt_text: Week plan from Monday to Friday with a 30-minute Friday check split into three 10-minute questions about views, saves and next week's focus.
